output.name: Nalsa

anatomy.part: head, centre of the gull's head at the top of the body, just behind the beak
right shoulder, where the neck meets the leading edge of the right wing
wing-root and belly, the join of the body's right edge to the underside of the right wing
right wingtip, the leading point of the swept right wing
right outer trailing tip, the far back corner of the right wing
right wing trailing edge, the feathers' inner end where the trailing edge turns back toward the body
left wingtip, raised high on the left wing
left wing outer edge, where the wing turns back down toward the tail
left wing trailing edge, the lowest feathers of the left wing
left wing inner trailing edge, where the feathers come in toward the tail
tail, the knot at the base of the body where the fan of tail feathers spreads

output.myth: When Aun cut the string, the Gale Tavo caught the first kite that had flown too close to the cut and tore its wings. Ennu the Kite-Wright found it in the surf under the cliffs, cold and bent, and sat up three nights with cloth and whalebone. Ennu stitched the tail back on with sinew, bent the wings to the shape a gull holds when it turns into the wind, and set it aloft. The Gulls went out to see whether it would fly. It did, badly, then well, and it has been circling over the north ever since, never quite coming down. Hesk counts it on the Reel each winter. Its tail is the bright knot Tesk, where Ennu's last stitch went. If you are caught in a gale on the water, look up and find the bird with the mended wing. It does not come down for prayers, but it turns, and a boat that is turned has room to live.
output.verse:
Stitched tail, bent wing bone,
the gull turns in Tavo's gale,
a turned boat has room.
